transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Um... well, I guess it's my eating. Just... doing too much of it, I suppose. 

Like, after my late shifts, I'll stop and get takeout on the way back. I usually end up eating, you know, two burgers, fries, a shake... and then I still go home and just sort of... clean out whatever leftovers are in the fridge out in the garage. Like it's a whole second supper. So... yeah. That's why I'm here.
Do you usually feel stressed, anxious, or upset before eating this much food?

Um... I don't think so. Not really. 

I mean, work is just work. I'm mostly just... tired from the shift, I guess. I haven't really noticed feeling upset or anything like that.
Do you feel like you can stop eating once you've started on those late nights?

No. Um... not really. 

It's... I don't know, once I start, it just feels like a switch gets flipped, I guess. I'll even be sitting there telling myself, you know, 'Roy, just shut the bag and go inside.' But... my hands just keep reaching for more. So... yeah. I don't really stop.
Do you usually feel guilty after eating that much food?

Yeah. Um... yeah, I do. 

It's... I guess I feel pretty ashamed afterward. Kind of disgusted with myself, honestly. I've just... I've always thought of myself as a disciplined guy, you know? Dependable. So... doing that, sneaking around my own garage to eat... it just feels like I'm really letting myself down.
Do you feel like you're in control while you're eating all that food on those late nights?

Um... like I was just saying... no. I don't. 

It's... it's just like that switch I mentioned. My brain is telling me to quit, but... I just keep going anyway. So... no. Not really in control.
Do you find yourself eating this way every time you have a late shift?

Um... not every time, no. But... yeah, for the last few months, it's been... maybe once a week. Sometimes two or three times, if it's been a rough day on the line or... you know, a late shift. So... yeah. Often enough, I guess.
Do you feel a sense of relief or comfort while you're eating on those late nights?

Um... I don't know. I haven't really... paid attention to that. 

I guess I don't really think about how I'm feeling when it's happening. I'm just... doing it. So... I'm not sure.
Do you think you would eat this way if you weren't feeling tired after your late shifts?
Um... hard to say. I'm pretty much always tired after work, so... I don't really know. I haven't thought about it.
Do you think you would eat this way if you weren't tired after your late shifts, or is the tiredness triggering something else that leads to eating?

I mean... like I just said, I'm pretty much always beat after a shift. So I don't really have anything to compare it to. 

I don't know about it triggering anything else. I just... I get home, and it happens. I haven't really analyzed it beyond that.
Do you think you would eat this way if you weren't alone when you got home from your late shifts?

Well... probably not, no. 

I... I usually make sure I'm alone. Like, even at dinner with my wife, I'll... act like I'm just not that hungry. And then later on, I'll go out to the truck, or... or just wait until she's busy doing something else. 

I just... I'd be embarrassed for her to see how much I'm putting away. So... yeah.
Do you think you would eat this way if you weren't feeling any emotional upset or stress at all?

I don't know. I don't really... think about it like that. 

I'm not really an emotional guy, so... I couldn't tell you. Work is just work, you know? I haven't really noticed if stress has anything to do with it. Like I said, it just kind of happens.
Do you feel physically hungry when you start eating on those late nights?
I don't know. I guess... maybe sometimes? But usually, no. I'm just... eating. I don't really pay attention to whether my stomach is actually growling or anything like that.
Do you think you would still eat this way if you weren't feeling tired or anything else, but were feeling upset or anxious?
I... I really couldn't say. Like I told you, I'm just not one to get all worked up or anxious about things. So I don't know what I'd do in that situation. It's just not something that happens to me.
Do you think your eating behavior on those late nights is related to trying to cope with any difficult emotions?
Look, I... no. I don't think so. Like I just said, I don't really have those kinds of difficult emotions to cope with. I'm just eating. I don't think it's anything deep like that.
Do you think you would still eat this way if you weren't feeling tired after your shifts, but were feeling bored or had nothing else to do?
I mean... I don't know. I guess I'm just usually working or sleeping, so... I don't really get bored much. I just... I don't really know if I'd do it then.
Do you think you would eat this way if someone was with you the entire time after you got home from your late shifts?

No. I... probably not. 

I usually... well, like with my wife, I'll act like I'm not really hungry at dinner. I wait until she's busy with something, or I'll just go out to the truck later on. I just wouldn't want her to see how much I'm putting away. It'd be... I guess I'd be embarrassed. 

So, no. If someone was right there with me, I wouldn't do it.
Do you think being alone after your late shifts plays a role in why you eat this way?
I guess so. I mean... yeah, probably. It's just... it's easier when nobody's around. I don't know if it's the whole reason, but... yeah. That's just when I do it.
Do you feel like you're eating this way out of habit or because you feel like you need to?

I don't know if it's a habit, exactly. It's just... well, once I start, it feels like a switch gets flipped. 

I'll even be sitting there telling myself... Roy, shut the bag and go inside. Just put it away. But... my hands just keep reaching for more anyway. I don't really know what you'd call that.
Do you think you would still eat this way if you weren't feeling any negative emotions about yourself after eating?

I don't know. I just... I don't feel good about it. 

I've always been a guy who does what he's supposed to do. Dependable, you know? Disciplined. And then... I'm out there in the truck, sneaking around. 

After I do it, I just feel... ashamed, I guess. Disgusted with myself. It feels like I'm letting myself down. So, I don't know if the feelings cause it, or if they just come after. I just know they're there.
Do you feel like you're eating this way because you feel compelled to, or because it's a way for you to deal with something else?
I don't really know. I haven't thought about it like that. It's just... something that happens. I don't know if I'm dealing with anything.
